speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I see you've been experiencing knee pain after increasing your physical activity. To help me understand better, can you tell me exactly where on your knee the pain is located, and does it feel sharp, dull, or throbbing?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. She cites recent participation in volleyball involving repetitive pivoting and twisting movements as a possible cause. She was advised at her last physical exam that weight loss could be beneficial for her health.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for those details. To narrow this down, does the pain feel like it's specifically inside the joint or more on the outer or inner side, and have you noticed any swelling or hearing a "pop" when you first started playing?

REQUEST IMAGES: Knee_MRI (focusing on MCL and meniscus)

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Knee pain, specifically over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella. I also have Recent weight loss attempt, Increased physical activity. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is a very specific location. Did you experience any significant swelling in that area, or does the pain worsen specifically when you try to twist your knee or press directly on that spot?

REQUEST TEST: Physical_Exam_Assessment (checking for joint line tenderness and effusion)

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Physical Examination reveals tenderness over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella upon palpation. There is no visible swelling, erythema, or appreciable joint effusion noted. The patient reports no significant limitation in range of motion or ligamentous instability.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome (Shin Splints)
